subject: Re: Encord x Streetscope
text:
I appreciate the time you guys took and agree we might be closer to being a customer at some point downstream. 

My last question for you was serious, albeit rushed. Given requirements for secrecy, especially in the AV sector, I don’t know enough about how training is done. Our thesis is that our data stream, highly structured data that characterizes safe / hazardous driving, would be highly valuable to those building/training foundational models. Is this something Encord would be interested in selling to its AV customers? Is there a way we can partner to do that? subject: Re: Encord/Tau Robotics - Services for G1_Mobile Project
text:
Hi Dave,

I’ve reviewed 7 episodes — overall, they’re quite good. There were only one
or two scores I would adjust by more than 2 points.
My main feedback points are:

   - The humanoid still walks quite slowly and loudly, so it generally
   cannot reach a score of 4 (“good”). If it successfully navigates to the
   target, it usually deserves a 3 (“ok”).
   - When the humanoid touches or bumps into objects, it often applies
   excessive force — for example, pushing against a shelf or grasping the
   cookies too tightly.
   - It should start executing the task promptly once the instruction
   begins. A customer shouldn’t have to wait 10 seconds before it moves.

Some variation is inevitable, but please aim to make scores as
deterministic and reproducible as possible. Try to rate as an average human
evaluator would if told:
“You’ve bought this humanoid and given it these task instructions. How
happy are you with its execution?”
Later, we may have multiple annotators label the same episodes to further
calibrate consistency.

Best,
Alex
